newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - calendar big, inflows small.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - calendar big, inflows small.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to up 1/4 point by midday as players eyed next week's beefy calendar, including big competitive deals from New Jersey and California.
Eighty-eight competitive deals totaling $2.4 billion are scheduled for next week, while 61 negotiated deals totaling $2.52 billion are expected.

Deals are set to arrive against a backdrop of only modest cash inflows into municipal bond funds. According to one market source, AMG Data Services reported inflows of $17.688 million during the latest reporting week.
Friday's market was quiet, traders said.
"I don't think the market is really focused on anything except the calendar next week," one trader said. "New Jersey Trans and Cal, that's where the focus is going to be."
New Jersey Transportation Fund Authority is slated to sell $713 million of bonds competitively at 1100 EDT Wednesday. California's $500 million offering is scheduled for 1200 EDT Tuesday.

Next week's negotiated deals include a $459 million New City Transit Authority deal via Dillon Read & Co and a $211 million Chicago O'Hare Airport, Ill., offering through Bear Stearns & Co. Bear Stearns is also slated to bring a $175 million Texas Housing deal.
A second trader said Thursday's deals "went very well," and that next week's "decent" calendar should help the market.
"It's probably going to create a little more opportunity than there has been in the market," he said.

Friday's actively quoted secondary issues included Intermountain Power Agency, Utah, supply revenue refunding bonds. The 5.0 percent bonds of July 2021 were bid at 5.79 percent versus 5.80 percent at Thursday's close.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 11/32 at 99-22/32 to yield 6.77 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 5/32 at 114-31/32. The December T-bond contract was up 9/32 at 111-13/32. The MOB spread was 114 ticks.
